title: Impact of the Administrative Reform on Public Servants
seoTitle: Impact of the Administrative Reform on Public Servants
subtitle: Understand the main changes in career, job security, and benefits for civil servants
excerpt: The administrative reform changes career structures, job security, and benefits, with new evaluation rules that reshape the daily work of public servants.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The administrative reform has sparked intense discussions about the future of public servants, promising structural changes that affect career, job security, and benefits. The debate gains momentum as proposals advance in Congress, raising doubts and expectations among the thousands of professionals working for the State.

New rules for career progression

The proposal introduces a progression model that prioritizes merit criteria, reducing the emphasis on length of service as the sole parameter. Employees will be evaluated based on productivity indicators, competency development, and contribution to institutional results. This shift aims to align professional advancement with actual performance, encouraging continuous training and the adoption of innovative practices in daily work.

Under the new logic, the creation of managerial positions or strategic roles may depend on internal selection processes, which require proof of experience and concrete results. Thus, meritocracy becomes the central axis of the advancement trajectory, offering greater transparency in promotion pathways.

Job security and the possibility of dismissal

One of the most debated points concerns job security, traditionally guaranteed after the probationary period. The reform proposes that security remains, but linked to periodic assessments that consider performance and conduct. If an employee fails to reach satisfactory levels, the continuation of the bond may be reviewed, allowing the public agency to adopt corrective measures or, in extreme cases, dismissal.

This flexibility aims to make the public service more agile and responsive, while preserving the legal certainty of workers who demonstrate commitment and consistent results. The change requires the creation of clear evaluation mechanisms so that the process is perceived as fair and predictable.

Performance evaluations as a central element

The new framework incorporates performance evaluations as a permanent management tool. Each employee will undergo evaluation cycles that combine quantitative targets, such as service output, and qualitative goals, like quality of citizen service. Feedback from these evaluations will guide individual development plans and serve as the basis for promotion decisions or job restructuring.

To ensure the system’s effectiveness, the proposal foresees the use of digital tools that enable real-time monitoring of performance indicators. This digitization enhances transparency, reduces bureaucracy, and allows managers and employees to access relevant information for decision-making.

Changes to benefits and working conditions

Beyond career matters, the reform includes adjustments to the benefits granted to employees. Among the planned changes, the revision of leave regimes, medical assistance, and pension plans stands out, with a focus on financial sustainability. The alterations aim to balance benefit provision with the need to maintain the State’s investment capacity.

Working conditions will also be affected. The proposal encourages the adoption of more flexible work regimes, such as teleworking, when compatible with the nature of the activity. This flexibility seeks to improve employees’ quality of life while increasing the efficiency of services delivered to the public.

Outlook for human resource management in the public sector

With the outlined changes, human-resource management in the public sector will require new leadership profiles capable of integrating performance evaluation, career planning, and benefit management. Managers will need to develop strategic competencies such as data analysis, conducting internal selection processes, and transparent communication with teams.

The future scenario points to a more results-oriented public service, where meritocracy and flexibility combine to attract and retain talent. Although the transition requires adjustments and training, the expectation is that the reform will contribute to modernizing administration, strengthening society’s confidence in public institutions.
